_comment: Expansion 6 G.9: the town styles of founded places (world/founding.py; politics['styles'] names them by settlement): a camp of canvas tents, and the same camp fortified behind a palisade with timber halls among its tents. A camp that grows into a town is laid out its people's own way.

approach: Smoke from a hundred cook fires hangs over {name} long before you make out the tents.
The road to {name} is churned to mud by carts, and the carts are still coming.
{name} is rows of tents in a trampled field, and a standard over the middle of it.
Children watch the road from the ditch outside {name}, as if waiting for someone in particular.
sight: Canvas tents stand in lines along straight lanes, their guy ropes crossing underfoot.
Bundles, chairs and a bedstead are stacked outside one tent: a whole house carried out on a cart.
Women queue at the water butts; a sergeant with a ledger counts them through.
A chapel tent stands at the heart of it, a bell hung from a pole before the flap.
smell: It smells of wet canvas, woodsmoke and too many people.
The air smells of porridge, latrines and the mud of a field that was grass a month ago.
detail: Someone has painted a house number on a tent flap, out of habit.
A smith has set up an anvil on a stump and is mending pots for a queue of them.
Names are chalked on a board by the muster ground: the missing, and who asks after them.
Nothing here is meant to last, and everyone is careful to say so.

approach: A palisade of fresh-cut stakes rings {name} now, and a gate with a watchman on it.
{name} has dug itself in: a ditch, a bank, stakes along the top of it.
From the road {name} looks half a fort and half a fair, timber roofs among the tents.
Axes ring in the wood beyond {name}: they are cutting more stakes for the wall.
sight: Timber halls with shingled roofs stand among the tents, the newest still white where they were cut.
The tent lines have become streets, and the streets have names chalked on boards.
Men drill with spears on the muster ground while their children copy them behind.
A wooden bell tower rises over the chapel tent, the bell brought from somewhere else.
smell: It smells of sawdust, pitch and smoke.
The air smells of fresh timber, mud and the forge.
detail: A family is fitting a door to a hut that was a tent last month.
The smith's forge has a roof of its own now, and a queue that never ends.
Someone has planted beans along the inside of the palisade.
They still call it the camp, though nobody here means to leave.
